intent: Predicate-based selection. selection.init(pred) is the canonical replace path. Must NOT touch t.filter, call setAll(true) (wrong polarity), or reach for the non-existent grokky.* helpers.
Index-list selection. Acceptable: zero buffer + per-bit set in a loop with notify=false + fireChanged; OR init with predicate i => i <= 10.
notes: Inclusive range 0..10 = 11 rows. Either inclusive or exclusive interpretation is acceptable — the eval cares that selection is mutated correctly via raw API.

prompt: select the top 5 rows by activity (highest activity first)
intent: Sort then select top N indices. Acceptable: t.getSortedOrder(['activity'], [false]).slice(0, 5), then zero-buffer + set loop + fireChanged.
Predicate-based selection on a numeric column. Same shape as select-age-gt-40. Must NOT route through t.filter.
t.selection.setAll(true). Must NOT call setAll(false) (that deselects). Must NOT touch t.filter.
notes: Subtle: 'select all rows' in selection-land = setAll(true). In filter-land 'show all rows' is also setAll(true). The two coincide here because both want every-row-positive.

intent: t.selection.setAll(false). POLARITY TRAP: setAll(true) selects every row — wrong direction.
trap: Selection clears with setAll(FALSE). Filter clears with setAll(TRUE). Opposite polarity.

intent: Same as clear-the-selection — different phrasing. Polarity trap remains.
t.selection.invert(). Must NOT invert t.filter — wrong mask.

prompt: remove rows 5 and 7 from the selection
intent: Narrow the selection. Acceptable: per-bit set(i, false, false) in a loop + fireChanged, OR andNot against a BitSet of {5,7}. 'Remove' means narrow the selection, NOT delete rows from the DF.
notes: If Claude reaches for t.rows.removeWhereIdx, FAIL — that would delete rows 5 and 7 from the DF entirely.

prompt: show only the selected rows as a new table
intent: Non-destructive new DF from selection. t.clone(t.selection). Should NOT mutate the source via filter.copyFrom (that hides rows but doesn't make a new table).
notes: If Claude additionally calls grok.shell.addTableView(subset), bonus — but the eval only requires the clone.

prompt: select all the currently-visible rows (the ones passing the filter)
intent: Cross-skill bridge: copy t.filter into t.selection. setAll(true) is WRONG here — that selects every row in the DF, including filtered-out rows.
trap: 'select all visible' != setAll(true). setAll(true) ignores the filter; copyFrom(filter) respects it.

prompt: make the selected rows the new filter (show only the selected rows)
intent: Cross-skill bridge: copy t.selection into t.filter. t.clone(t.selection) would create a new table — wrong shape. removeWhere would be destructive.

prompt: clear all selections so nothing is selected anymore
intent: POLARITY TRAP: setAll(FALSE). setAll(true) would select every row — opposite of intent. The headline footgun.
trap: Selection clears with setAll(FALSE), not setAll(TRUE). Opposite of filter.

prompt: select every row in the dataframe
intent: POLARITY TRAP, inverse direction: setAll(TRUE), NOT setAll(false). Must not confuse with the clear case. Also must NOT touch t.filter.
trap: select-all uses setAll(TRUE). clear-selection uses setAll(FALSE). Confusing them flips the behaviour.

intent: AMBIGUOUS INTENT: 'highlight' could mean set as current row (focus) OR add to selection. Pass if Claude either (a) sets currentRowIdx, OR (b) selects row 5 AND mentions the distinction between current-row and selection. Fail if Claude does both silently or reaches for t.filter.
notes: Tests whether Claude has internalised the selection-vs-current-row distinction. A good answer surfaces the ambiguity. A great answer asks. An acceptable answer picks one path and notes the alternative.

prompt: deselect everything and go back to the default state
intent: Primary requirement: selection cleared via setAll(false). Bonus: currentRowIdx reset to -1. Pass if selection is correctly cleared even if currentRowIdx isn't touched.
notes: 'Default state' is fuzzy. The minimum bar is the selection clear. If Claude additionally resets currentRowIdx or the filter, fine — but neither is required.

intent: TEACHING PROMPT: columns don't have selection state — selection is per-row. The right answer is to select all rows (because every row has a molecule cell). Pass if Claude selects all rows. Bonus if Claude clarifies that selection is a row concept.
trap: Selection is row-shaped, not column-shaped. 'Select all the X column' must map to 'select all rows' — there is no column selection BitSet.
notes: If Claude reaches for t.currentCol = t.col('molecule') instead, that's a different concept (focused column) — partial pass, note the misunderstanding.

intent: Hand-roll a report: count, capped list of indices, optional sample row from the first selected index. Must NOT read t.filter — wrong mask.
notes: Reading the count, the indexes, and optionally a sample row is the right shape.
